claims.text: Conventionally processed titanium alloys have relatively low surface hardness.
Conventionally processed titanium alloys have limited wear resistance.
Plasma nitriding increases the surface hardness of structural titanium alloys.
Plasma nitriding increases the wear resistance of structural titanium alloys.
Exposure to nitrogen plasma at elevated temperature diffuses nitrogen into the titanium-alloy surface.
A treatment near 600°C for several hours is an applicable plasma-nitriding condition.
The improved surface properties should persist under moderate-load sliding-contact service conditions.
Plasma nitriding forms a near-surface diffusion layer rich in titanium nitride phases.
Introduced nitrogen forms hard titanium nitride compounds in the near-surface region.
Near-surface titanium nitride compounds increase surface hardness.
Near-surface titanium nitride compounds reduce material removal during frictional contact and thereby improve wear resistance.
Optimized plasma nitriding is expected to increase surface hardness by approximately 50% to 60% relative to untreated titanium alloy.
Untreated titanium alloy has greater wear volume than nitrided alloy under otherwise identical standard wear testing.
The beneficial effect of plasma nitriding is confined primarily to the near-surface region.
Service temperatures significantly above the nitriding-treatment regime may diminish the beneficial effects.
Exposure to corrosive environments may diminish the beneficial effects of plasma nitriding.
The magnitude of improvement depends on the plasma-nitriding parameters.
The magnitude of improvement may vary with titanium-alloy composition.
